title: The Wizard of Oz · 2. The Scarecrow
source: Retold from L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), public domain. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/55

text: Dorothy put on the silver shoes, packed a basket of bread, and set off with Toto along the yellow brick road.
The shoes twinkled in the sun with every step.
pages.alt: Dorothy sets off on the yellow brick road with a basket

text: Beside a cornfield she saw a Scarecrow up on a pole.
To her surprise, one of its painted eyes slowly winked at her!
pages.alt: A scarecrow on a pole in the cornfield winks at Dorothy

text: "Good day," said the Scarecrow in a husky voice.
"Can you help me down? This pole is very uncomfortable."
pages.alt: The Scarecrow asks Dorothy for help

text: Dorothy lifted him off the pole. He was very light, because he was stuffed with straw.
"Thank you," he said. "I feel like a new man."
"I have no brains in my head, only straw," he sighed.
"Do you think the Wizard of Oz would give me some brains?"
pages.alt: The Scarecrow wishes he had brains

text: The crows had never been afraid of him, because they knew he was only straw.
"Come with me," said Dorothy. "We will ask the Wizard together."
So the Scarecrow and Dorothy and Toto walked on together.
The Scarecrow stumbled over the bricks and laughed, and Dorothy laughed with him.
pages.alt: Dorothy, Toto and the Scarecrow walk on together

questions.ask: Who did Dorothy find in the cornfield?
What was the Scarecrow stuffed with?
Which birds were not afraid of the Scarecrow?
